# package client

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-bacnet/client"
```

Package client implements a BACnet/IP supervisory client runtime.

One Client instance represents one local BACnet/IP data-link endpoint. The client composes bvlc → npdu → apdu → service layers.

	DefaultObservationTTL      = 30 * time.Minute
)
```

```

DeviceManagementConfirm is the exact confirmation string required by WithDeviceManagementEnabled.

#### func New

```go
func New(opts ...Option) (*Client, error)
```

New validates the options, opens the BACnet/IP UDP socket (unless WithTransport supplies a transport) and starts the receive loop. With WithForeignDevice it also starts registering with the BBMD in the background; New does not wait for the result (see ForeignDeviceRegistered).

An invalid option value fails with an error wrapping bacnet.ErrInvalidConfig; a socket that cannot be opened fails with the operating-system error. Close the returned Client to release the socket.

#### func (Client) Close

```go
func (c *Client) Close() error
```

Close stops the client and releases its socket. It is idempotent and safe to call concurrently with any other method.

Requests still waiting for a response return bacnet.ErrClosed, wrapped in \*bacnet.OutcomeUnknownError when the request was a write that had already been sent. COV subscriptions end with a Closed event and are not cancelled on the devices (they lapse with their lifetime); close each Subscription first to cancel it. A foreign-device registration is left to expire with its TTL. Close waits for the client's goroutines, so it must not be called from an EventNotification handler or a diagnostic callback.

#### func (Client) Discover

```go
func (c *Client) Discover(ctx context.Context, opts DiscoveryOptions) ([]DeviceObservation, error)
```

Discover broadcasts a Who-Is and collects the I-Am replies. The returned slice holds the devices seen since the call started, in no particular order; Devices() returns everything the registry still retains.

With opts.Window set, Discover returns after that time with a nil error. Without it, it collects until ctx ends and returns the devices together with ctx.Err(). In both cases the devices gathered so far are returned when ctx is cancelled or the client is closed (bacnet.ErrClosed).

The Who-Is is a global broadcast sent to the local IPv4 broadcast address (see WithInterface), or through the BBMD when registered as a foreign device. For peers a broadcast cannot reach, call SendWhoIs with their address and read Devices().

#### func (Client) ReadObjectList

```go
func (c *Client) ReadObjectList(ctx context.Context, target Target, object bacnet.ObjectIdentifier, maxItems int) ([]bacnet.ObjectIdentifier, error)
```

ReadObjectList reads the Object\_List of a Device object. maxItems caps the returned count (0 uses decode MaxElements).

The whole array is requested first. Devices that cannot return it in one reply (no segmentation, small buffer) abort that request; the list is then read element by element: the count from array index 0, the entries with ReadPropertyMultiple, or with one ReadProperty each when the device does not support ReadPropertyMultiple.

#### func (Client) ReadPropertyMultipleBatched

```go
func (c *Client) ReadPropertyMultipleBatched(ctx context.Context, target Target, specs []service.ReadAccessSpecification, opts RPMBatchOptions) ([]service.ReadAccessResult, error)
```

ReadPropertyMultipleBatched reads specs with as many ReadPropertyMultiple transactions as the peer's MaxAPDU requires and returns one result per input spec, in input order, with per-property errors preserved.

A batch holds at most MaxPropertiesPerBatch property references and never more than fit in one unsegmented request; a spec with many properties is split across batches and its results are joined again. When the peer aborts because the reply did not fit (buffer-overflow, segmentation-not-supported, apdu-too-long) the batch is halved and retried, which is safe because the service only reads. A single property whose value still does not fit is returned as that Abort.

On error the results gathered so far are returned with it; specs not yet read have no Properties.

#### func (Client) ReadRangeAll

```go
func (c *Client) ReadRangeAll(ctx context.Context, target Target, req service.ReadRangeRequest, opts ReadRangePageOptions) (ReadRangePageResult, error)
```

ReadRangeAll pages ReadRange until the peer reports LAST\_ITEM, returns an empty or short final page, or a configured limit is reached (Partial is then set and StoppedReason names the limit).

Only byPosition and bySequenceNumber are advanced automatically. byTime paging requires the caller to supply successive ReferenceTime values via repeated ReadRange calls.

When broadcast is true, the request uses Original-Broadcast-NPDU (or Distribute-Broadcast-To-Network when registered as a foreign device). #### func (Client) SubscribeCOV

```go
func (c *Client) SubscribeCOV(ctx context.Context, target Target, object bacnet.ObjectIdentifier, opts COVOptions) (Subscription, error)
```

SubscribeCOV subscribes to change-of-value notifications for object and returns once the device has accepted the subscription.

Read Events until it is closed. The first event reports the Active state; later events carry notifications or state changes (Renewing, Degraded when a renewal failed or events were dropped). Close cancels the subscription on the device and ends the stream with a Closed event; closing the Client ends it without cancelling. The Subscription is safe for concurrent use.

#### func (Client) SubscribeCOVMultiple

```go
func (c *Client) SubscribeCOVMultiple(ctx context.Context, target Target, specs []service.COVMultipleSubscription, opts COVMultipleOptions) (Subscription, error)
```

SubscribeCOVMultiple subscribes to changes of several properties of several objects with one SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple request and returns once the device has accepted it.

The Subscription behaves as the one SubscribeCOV returns: the client renews it at half the lifetime and Close cancels it on the device. Its notification events have Multiple set (and Notification nil): one event per COVNotificationMultiple, with the notification's timestamp and, for properties subscribed with Timestamped, each value's time of change. Objects the subscription did not ask for are left out, and a notification with none of its objects is dropped.

specs is copied. A device that does not implement the service answers with a \*bacnet.RejectError (unrecognized-service).

### type EventNotificationHandler

```go
type EventNotificationHandler func(EventNotificationDelivery)
```

EventNotificationHandler receives decoded EventNotifications.

Confirmed notifications are SimpleACK'd before the handler is invoked. The handler runs synchronously on the receive path: it must not block and must not call Client methods that wait for a response (ReadProperty, confirmed requests, Discover, etc.), or the receive loop can deadlock. Prefer copying the delivery and handling work on another goroutine. Handler panics are recovered so a faulty callback cannot stop reception.

### type ForeignDeviceConfig

```go
type ForeignDeviceConfig struct {
	BBMD bip.Endpoint
	TTL  time.Duration
}
```

ForeignDeviceConfig registers with a single BBMD.

TTL must be a whole number of seconds and at least 2s (wire encoding is uint16 seconds). Zero selects the default of 60s. Wire TTL and renew scheduling both use the normalized whole-second value.

BVLC-Result correlation is by pending attempt and BBMD peer only: the wire has no generation field, so a delayed Result for an earlier attempt at the same BBMD cannot be distinguished from a Result for the current attempt.

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*config)
```

Option configures a Client.

#### func WithAdvertisedMaxAPDU

```go
func WithAdvertisedMaxAPDU(size uint16) Option
```

WithAdvertisedMaxAPDU sets the Max APDU length accepted field in confirmed requests. When 0 (default), the client advertises DecodeLimits.MaxAPDUSize.

Validated at New: 0 or ≥ 50, encodable as a BACnet MaxAPDU code, and not greater than DecodeLimits.MaxAPDUSize. Non-discrete values floor to the next lower defined size when encoded (50/128/206/480/1024/1476).

Use a value smaller than DecodeLimits.MaxAPDUSize to coax peers into segmenting ComplexACK responses without tightening the local parser bound. Some peers size segment payloads to the advertised maximum without reserving APDU header space; keeping the decode limit higher avoids dropping those segments.

#### func WithDecodeLimits

```go
func WithDecodeLimits(l bacnet.DecodeLimits) Option
```

WithDecodeLimits sets parser/reassembly limits.

#### func WithDeviceManagementEnabled

```go
func WithDeviceManagementEnabled(confirm string) Option
```

WithDeviceManagementEnabled opts into DeviceCommunicationControl and ReinitializeDevice (OperationDeviceManagement). confirm must equal DeviceManagementConfirm; any other value makes New fail.

These services can disable communication or reboot a peer. Exact-APDU retransmission is disabled and post-send timeout/cancel returns \*bacnet.OutcomeUnknownError.

#### func WithDiagnosticFunc

```go
func WithDiagnosticFunc(fn func(Diagnostic)) Option
```

WithDiagnosticFunc registers a callback for client diagnostics: malformed or unexpected frames, responses that match no transaction, route and foreign-device changes, dropped queue entries. See OBSERVABILITY.md for the kinds.

The callback is invoked synchronously on the receive and timeout paths, possibly from several goroutines. It must return promptly, must not panic and must not call back into the Client. Nil removes the callback. It may be combined with WithLogger.

#### func WithEventDispatcher

```go
func WithEventDispatcher(cfg EventDispatcherConfig) Option
```

WithEventDispatcher enables a bounded asynchronous EventNotification worker pool. Confirmed notifications are still SimpleACK'd on the receive path before enqueue. Handler must be non-nil. When set, the synchronous WithEventNotificationHandler path is unused for deliveries (dispatcher owns the handler). OpenEventStream remains independent.

#### func WithEventNotificationHandler

```go
func WithEventNotificationHandler(h EventNotificationHandler) Option
```

WithEventNotificationHandler registers a handler for inbound Confirmed/Unconfirmed EventNotification PDUs. Confirmed notifications are SimpleACK'd before the handler runs. Nil disables the handler.

The handler is invoked synchronously on the receive path and must return promptly without panicking. Prefer WithEventDispatcher for asynchronous work.

#### func WithForeignDevice

```go
func WithForeignDevice(fd ForeignDeviceConfig) Option
```

WithForeignDevice enables foreign-device registration with one BBMD.

#### func WithInterface

```go
func WithInterface(name string) Option
```

WithInterface restricts subnet-directed broadcasts to one network interface (UDP transport only).

A broadcast is sent as one datagram to the directed broadcast address of each local subnet and one to the limited broadcast 255.255.255.255 on each interface (on Linux and macOS; elsewhere the system sends the limited broadcast once, on the interface of the default route). The subnets are those of the interface named here, or without this option of every interface that is up, broadcast-capable and not a loopback (only the subnet of the bound address when WithLocalAddr binds a specific one). Both forms are sent because devices differ in which one their socket receives; a device that receives both answers twice.

#### func WithLocalAddr

```go
func WithLocalAddr(addr string) Option
```

WithLocalAddr sets the UDP bind address (e.g. "0.0.0.0:47808"). Binding a specific unicast address stops most operating systems from delivering broadcast I-Am replies to the socket; prefer the wildcard address and WithInterface. Port 0 binds an ephemeral port, which works for unicast requests but not for peers that answer Who-Is by broadcast to 47808.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger logs client diagnostics through l. The client is silent without it: nil (the default) disables logging, and slog.Default is never used.

Each entry has the message of the diagnostic, a "kind" attribute and the diagnostic's fields. Frames the client drops (malformed, wrong source, no matching transaction) are logged at Debug; lost functionality (receive failures, foreign-device registration, dropped notifications, evictions) at Warn; route changes at Info. No payloads are logged.

#### func WithNetworkManagementEnabled

```go
func WithNetworkManagementEnabled(confirm string) Option
```

WithNetworkManagementEnabled opts into BVLC Write-BDT and similar OperationNetworkManagement actions. confirm must equal NetworkManagementConfirm; any other value makes New fail.

#### func WithPort

```go
func WithPort(port int) Option
```

WithPort sets the BACnet/IP UDP port the client binds and broadcasts to (default 47808). Zero selects the default; a port outside 0..65535 makes New fail. WithLocalAddr overrides the bind address but not the broadcast port.

#### func WithRegistryOptions

```go
func WithRegistryOptions(opts RegistryOptions) Option
```

WithRegistryOptions configures device-observation retention bounds. Zero fields select package defaults (see RegistryOptions).

#### func WithSegmentWindow

```go
func WithSegmentWindow(window uint8) Option
```

WithSegmentWindow sets both the send proposed window and the receive actual window. Production defaults keep receive at 1 for peer compatibility while proposing 16 on send; use this option when both directions should share a larger window. A window outside 1..127 makes New fail.

#### func WithTransactionOptions

```go
func WithTransactionOptions(apduTimeout time.Duration, retryCount int, segmentTimeout time.Duration) Option
```

WithTransactionOptions sets the APDU timeout (default 3s), the number of retransmissions after the first attempt (default 3) and the segment timeout (default 2s). A zero timeout keeps the default; retryCount 0 disables retransmission. A negative value makes New fail.

Retransmission only applies to services that are safe to repeat (reads); see ConfirmedServicePolicy. Without a context deadline a read that gets no answer fails with bacnet.ErrTimeout after apduTimeout × (retryCount + 1).

#### func WithTransport

```go
func WithTransport(t Transport) Option
```

WithTransport runs the client on t instead of opening a UDP socket. The client takes ownership: Close closes t, and New closes it when construction fails.

### type Subscription

```go
type Subscription interface {
	Events() <-chan SubscriptionEvent

```

Subscription is a COV subscription with explicit lifetime.

### type SubscriptionEvent

```go
type SubscriptionEvent struct {
	Sequence     uint64
	Notification *service.COVNotification
	Multiple     *service.COVNotificationMultiple
	State        SubscriptionState
	Gap          bool
	Err          error
}
```

SubscriptionEvent is a unified COV event.

Sequence is monotonic per subscription for successfully queued events. Gap is sticky: when one or more events were dropped due to a full queue, the next successfully delivered event has Gap=true so callers observe the loss.

Notification is set for a COV notification of a SubscribeCOV or SubscribeCOVProperty subscription. Multiple is set when the device sent a COVNotificationMultiple: it is the whole notification, with its timestamp and each value's time of change, and is all an event of a SubscribeCOVMultiple subscription carries. Both point to values that are not modified after delivery; Multiple may be shared between events.

### type Target

```go
type Target struct {
	Address  bacnet.Address
	Endpoint bip.Endpoint // immediate B/IP peer (device or router); required
	Origin   bip.Endpoint // optional forwarded origin expectation
	// MaxAPDU is the largest APDU the device accepts. Zero uses the value
	// from its I-Am when the device was discovered, else a conservative 480.
	MaxAPDU uint16
}
```

Target identifies a remote BACnet device for confirmed requests.

For a device reachable directly over BACnet/IP, Endpoint alone is enough: a zero Address is filled in as the local station at that endpoint. For a device behind a BACnet router, Address is the remote station (network and MAC) and Endpoint is the router; see ResolveTarget. DeviceObservation.Target builds either form from a discovery result.

Responses are only accepted from the path the Target describes.
